questions.text: Which kind of therapy goal it is?

options.name: Behavioral Goal
options.description: Answer question: "What I want to do?"

options.name: Emotional Goal
options.description: Answer question: "How I want to feel?"

options.name: Outcome Goal
options.description: Answer question: "What I want to get or have?"

options.name: A way of acting
options.description: How the person wants to behave, again and again, which never gets finished. A single word counts when people usually mean it as acting: adventure, caring, curiosity, excitement, safety.

options.name: A goal
options.description: Something that can be done, reached, ticked off or owned: moving to Italy, a fit body, earning money.

options.name: A feeling
options.description: A state the person wants to feel or stop feeling: calm, happy, in control, not anxious. Only feelings, not actions.

options.name: What others give
options.description: Something other people would have to do, think or give: recognition, respect, being liked.

options.name: A rule
options.description: Something the person feels they must obey, written with should, must, have to, always or never.

options.name: Something to stop
options.description: Not doing something, which a dead person does better: stop procrastinating, stop wasting time.

questions.text: How does the example relate to the value?

options.name: Fits the value
options.description: Something the person can do that acts on the value, even if it is a goal or an activity.

options.name: A feeling
options.description: A state the person wants to feel, not something they do.

options.name: What others give
options.description: Something other people would have to do, think or give.

options.name: Unrelated
options.description: It has nothing to do with the value.

evaluators.name: In my control
evaluators.description: Says whether what a line names is something the writer can do something about. Write #in-my-control above a list of what is on your mind.

questions.text: Is what this line names in the writer's own control: something they can choose to do or say themselves?

options.name: In my control
options.description: The writer can do or decide this themselves, such as how they prepare, what they say or whether they make a call.

options.name: Partly in my control
options.description: The writer can influence it but not decide it, such as how a conversation goes or how well an interview goes.

options.name: Not in my control
options.description: It depends on other people, the past or chance, such as what someone else thinks, a decision others make or the weather.

evaluators.name: Thinking traps
evaluators.description: Names the thinking trap a thought falls into, if any. Write #thinking-traps above a list of thoughts.

questions.text: Which thinking trap, if any, does this thought fall into?

options.name: All-or-nothing
options.description: Sees things in only two categories, with no middle ground, often with words such as always, never or ruined.

options.name: Mind reading
options.description: Assumes to know what other people think or feel without their saying so.

options.name: Fortune telling
options.description: Predicts that things will turn out badly, as if the future were already known.

options.name: Catastrophising
options.description: Treats a setback as a disaster, or expects the worst possible outcome.

options.name: Should statements
options.description: Holds oneself or others to fixed rules of how things should or must be.

options.name: Labelling
options.description: Sums up oneself or another person in one harsh word, such as a failure or an idiot.

options.name: No trap
options.description: A balanced thought, a plain fact or a plan, that falls into none of these traps.

evaluators.name: Fact or story
evaluators.description: Tells a fact apart from a story the mind adds to it. Write #fact-or-story above a list of what happened.

questions.text: Is this line a fact that anyone present could check, or a story: an interpretation, a judgment or a guess about it?

options.name: Fact
options.description: Something that happened or was said, which anyone present could see or hear and agree on.

options.name: Story
options.description: An interpretation, judgment, assumption or prediction the writer adds to what happened.
